memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "With the bull offer a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil; with the ram, two-tenths; and with each of the seven lambs, one-tenth. Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering for atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, and their drink offerings." - Num 29:9-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the Day of Atonement, alongside the burnt offerings, there was the special "sin offering for atonement." This was the heart of the day, the sacrifice by which the sins of the whole nation were symbolically covered and the people reconciled to God. Everything about this day centred on dealing with sin so that fellowship with a holy God could continue.

The careful provision God made for atonement reveals both His holiness and His mercy. His holiness meant that sin could not simply be ignored; it had to be dealt with. His mercy meant that He Himself provided the way for atonement to be made. God did not leave His people in their sin but graciously opened a path to reconciliation.

Yet the very repetition of this yearly atonement showed its limits. Year after year the same offerings had to be made, because the blood of bulls and goats could never truly take away sins (Heb 10:4). These sacrifices were pictures, faithful shadows pointing to a reality they could not themselves provide. Something greater was needed.

That greater reality is Christ. He is both our perfect High Priest and the perfect sacrifice, who by one offering has made us holy forever (Heb 10:10). The atonement Israel could only picture year by year, He has accomplished once and for all. In Him our sin is not merely covered but taken away completely. Rejoice in the full and final atonement made by the Son of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How do you see both God's holiness and His mercy in the Day of Atonement?
2. Why could the yearly sacrifices never fully take away sin?
3. What does it mean that Christ's atonement is full and final?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are both my High Priest and my perfect sacrifice. Thank You that by Your one offering my sin is not merely covered but taken away completely. I rejoice in Your full atonement. Amen.
